items.title: 13.2.3 Nature of Excretory Products in relation to Habitat

source_refs.note: Topic 13.2.3 with the uric acid box (PDF 6-7).

blocks.text: In many animals osmoregulation is linked with removing nitrogenous wastes, which are excreted dissolved in water. The form of waste depends on how much water the habitat allows.

blocks.caption: Nitrogenous wastes
rows: Ammonia (NH3): formed in the liver when amino groups removed from amino acids and nucleic acids combine with H+
highly toxic; about 500 mL of water per gram
ammonotelic: most fishes, protozoans, sponges, coelenterates; marine animals release it straight into the water
Urea, CO(NH2)2: made from ammonia in the liver
less toxic; about 50 mL per gram
Uric acid, C5H4N4O3: made from ammonia using much energy; forms precipitates
least toxic and less soluble; about 1 mL per gram
uricotelic: insects, desert animals, birds, most reptiles

blocks.text: Humans also excrete a little uric acid, a by-product of breaking down purines from foods such as meat. When there is too much uric acid in the blood, crystals can form in joints and tissues, causing the painful condition called gout.
